Severe leptospirosis carries a 50% mortality rate; early antibiotic treatment can improve outcomes.

article.articleHeadline: Doctors caution against indiscriminate antibiotic use as monsoon-related illnesses rise
article.articleSummary: Doctors caution against indiscriminate antibiotic use as monsoon-related illnesses rise. With fever as a common symptom, clinicians warn that fever does not reliably indicate a bacterial infection and self-medication with antibiotics can fuel antimicrobial resistance. Viral illnesses, dengue, malaria, typhoid and other conditions can cause fever, and treatment should be guided by clinical assessment, duration of illness, associated symptoms, and appropriate diagnostic investigations. Patients often present after taking multiple medicines, including antibiotics, simply because they have fever; the first step is to determine the underlying cause rather than reflexively prescribing antibiotics. Antibiotics act against bacteria and have no effect on viral infections. These recommendations come from Dr Sujeet K Choudhary, Chief Medical Officer, Internal Medicine, Sitaram Bhartia Institute of Science and Research, urging rational antibiotic use during the monsoon season.

article.articleSummary: Eight-year-old Lilian Smart of the United States died after infection with Naegleria fowleri, the brain-eating amoeba. The girl contracted the parasite after swimming in the warm waters of Lake Kleiborno in Louisiana. She had been hospitalized since August 15, and on August 19 the state health department confirmed Naegleria fowleri infection. According to the U.S. CDC, since 1937 there have been about 180 reported Naegleria fowleri infections in the United States. The amoeba thrives in warm freshwater; infection occurs when water enters the nose, allowing the organism to reach the brain and cause primary amebic meningoencephalitis (PAM), a severe and nearly always fatal condition. Worldwide, most cases occur in southern, tropical climates, including the United States (notably the southern states), India, Pakistan, and Papua New Guinea; in Europe such cases are rare but generate strong public-health concern.

article.articleHeadline: Computational drug repurposing identifies dual-site inhibitors of the Kyasanur Forest disease virus NS3 helicase targeting its ATPase and RNA-binding domains
article.articleSummary: Kyasanur Forest Disease Virus (KFDV) NS3 helicase is evaluated as a dual-site inhibitor target in this in silico study, aiming at both the catalytic ATP-binding site (ABS) and the RNA-binding site (RBS). In India, KFDV remains an emerging threat with recurrent outbreaks and limited antiviral options. A structure-based drug repurposing screen of 9,716 DrugBank compounds using hierarchical docking (HTVS, SP, XP) identified promising complexes, which were further analyzed by 300 ns molecular dynamics simulations and post-simulation assessments (MM/GBSA, energy landscapes). The prodrug Taribavirin exhibited stable binding interactions and favorable energetics across both ABS and RBS, achieving dual-site engagement though not the top binder at either site. This study provides the first in silico evidence of dual-site NS3hel inhibition, proposing Taribavirin as a candidate for subsequent in vitro and in vivo validation.

article.articleHeadline: Hantavirus: a Lancet publication highlights Argentina's response to the cruise ship outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Argentina, led by ANLIS Malbrán, analyzes its hantavirus response to the MV Hondius cruise outbreak, which began after the ship departed Ushuaia on April 1, 2026. The Andes virus caused hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. Argentina conducted epidemiological and environmental investigations in Tierra del Fuego, Mendoza, and Neuquén, with Mendoza involving US CDC collaborators for rodent studies. Internationally, Argentina shared surveillance and diagnostic expertise, providing Andes virus RNA, RT-PCR controls, positive sera, ELISA plates, monoclonal antibodies, and diagnostic protocols to 13 countries — the Netherlands, United Kingdom, Spain, Philippines, Australia, South Korea, Malaysia, Nepal, Myanmar, Bangladesh, India, Senegal, and South Africa — with expansion to eight more. Nearly 6,000 diagnostic determinations were enabled abroad using these resources. The Lancet publication frames the Hondius episode as both a stress test for Latin America’s preparedness and a demonstration of meaningful national capacities and international cooperation, while underscoring remaining regional coordination gaps and advocating a regional rapid-response platform alongside PAHO.

article.articleHeadline: Study reveals prevalence and co-resistance of multidrug-resistant E. coli
article.articleSummary: From Chennai, India, a cross-sectional study of 1,356 urinary E. coli isolates collected Oct 2023–Mar 2024 found that 70.5% met the study’s definition of multidrug resistance. Resistance was strongest to nalidixic acid, ampicillin, and ticarcillin; extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) production occurred in 35.3% of isolates. A co-resistance network revealed tight connections centered on those three antibiotics, implying shared resistance determinants or clonal spread. The investigators used VITEK2 GN-235 for automated susceptibility testing and logistic regression to assess associations, reporting a positive relationship between patient age and fluoroquinolone resistance. The findings highlight mounting antimicrobial resistance in community-associated urinary infections and the utility of network analyses to guide surveillance and stewardship, underscoring pressing treatment challenges in India and beyond.

article.articleHeadline: The $6.1 Billion Question: Why Demand for Pathogen Culture Media Keeps Growing | Infection Control Today
article.articleSummary: Global selective culture media for pathogen detection is projected to reach $6.1 billion by 2035, up from $3.2 billion in 2026, driven by antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and stringent regulatory testing in clinical diagnostics, food safety, and pharmaceutical QC. AMR remains the primary catalyst, with WHO’s 2024 Priority Pathogen List of 24 pathogens and GLASS surveillance reinforcing demand for culture-based identification and susceptibility testing. Food-safety targets include Salmonella, Campylobacter, and Listeria; pharmaceutical quality control increases need for validated media. North America accounted for about 49% of the market in 2025 (~$1.4B); India and China are expanding lab networks. Challenges include competition from molecular methods and VBNC pathogens, plus supply-chain costs. Opportunities arise with ready-to-use, chromogenic media and underpenetrated markets in Latin America, Southeast Asia, India, and China, supported by AMR surveillance and regulatory frameworks (FSMA, FSIS).

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Ituri: decrease in community deaths in Niania
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in Ituri's Niania health zone shows a progressive decline in community deaths. Currently four community deaths per day, down from about ten per day a month ago in the PK 51 mining area and environs. The improvement follows better adherence to barrier measures and strengthened prevention, including suspension of cross-border traffic between Ituri and Haut-Uele and halting traffic between Mambasa (Ituri) and Wamba (Haut-Uele). About 50% of the population were displaced to Haut-Uele and Tshopo previously. Community leaders intensified awareness; more suspected cases are reported and fast-tracked to care. MSF is building a new treatment center at Niania and an isolation center at PK 47 to improve patient management and enable earlier detection and treatment in facilities.

article.articleHeadline: Hunting down the last cases of sleeping sickness
article.articleSummary: Sleeping sickness (gambiense human African trypanosomiasis, gHAT) remains in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with 471 cases worldwide in 2025, most in the DRC; WHO aims to end transmission by 2030. Mobile health teams pursue the last cases using a screen-and-treat strategy: anyone with a positive screening test is treated with acoziborole, a single-dose oral drug (three tablets) under supervision, without waiting for parasite confirmation. Confirmatory lab testing is still sent for some cases, but the simplified approach could enable community-level treatment where labs are scarce. Acoziborole shows about 98.1% efficacy in trials and was endorsed by EMA earlier this year. The EU-funded STROGHAT trial, led by Dr. Elena Nicco (ITM Antwerp) with Belgium, France, Switzerland and the DRC, seeks to accelerate elimination by reducing reliance on invasive procedures and hospital-based care. DNDi developed acoziborole.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in the DRC: Kinshasa barricades itself as best as it can against the spread of the virus - RTBF Actus
article.articleSummary: EBOLA outbreak in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo, with authorities deploying measures to curb spread, echoing Covid-era responses. Travel surveillance hinges on travelers' declarations, while prevention operates at two speeds: handwashing and barrier measures in hotels and supermarkets, but not in nightlife venues, markets, or poorer neighborhoods. Widespread clandestine ports and dilapidated roads hinder controls; an ill traveler could enter the capital via unmonitored routes and prompt transmission before detection. Public debate reveals belief in evil forces or denial that Ebola exists. Prevention messaging is concentrated among intellectuals and media circles, with less uptake among poorer communities where fake news circulates. Attitudes toward vaccination for a potential new strain remain uncertain, raising questions about acceptance of an eventual vaccine.

triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国の首都キンシャサ（人口密集地）で発生しており、監視体制の不備や住民の否認・偽情報拡散により感染拡大リスクが高いため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: a British professor in Bunia for studies aimed at strengthening the response.
article.articleSummary: British epidemiologist John Edmunds arrived in Bunia, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, with a World Health Organization delegation to bolster the Ebola virus disease (EVD) response. Meeting with military governor and alongside WHO Emergencies Director Dr. Chikwe Ihekweazu, the mission aims to strengthen response operations and support field health teams, with local actors evaluating the situation and scaling interventions to contain transmission. On the vaccination front, CEPI’s Aurélia Guyanne provided guidance on the vaccination strategy within the response. Edmunds’ presence is to generate new data to guide interventions and improve outbreak control. As of 25 August 2026, more than 2,500 deaths have been recorded across the six provinces affected by the outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Football, Cancer and Ebola
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to claim lives, with approximately 200 infections and 2,476 deaths reported. Melanoma research offers hope through a personalized mRNA-based therapeutic vaccine. Two faces of science emerge: a deadly outbreak with limited tools, and researchers making progress against one of society's great enemies. The piece urges reflection on priorities, noting that football chatter distracts from frontline scientists and health workers saving lives. As of August 26, 2026, the report emphasizes ongoing Ebola transmission while cancer research advances. Exact figures reflect a toll on communities and health systems, underscoring the need for sustained surveillance, vaccines, and therapeutics. Meanwhile, the melanoma vaccine advances illustrate how personalized immunotherapies, driven by RNA technology, may transform outcomes. By Ander Murillo (Ordizia).

article.articleHeadline: 4,630 cases of rabies-transmitting animal bites occurred in Denpasar, Bali in 2026; VAR stock is safe.
article.articleSummary: Rabies-transmitting animal bites in Denpasar, Bali reached 4,630 cases treated from January to June 2026. Anti-rabies vaccine (VAR) stock is considered safe as of 24 August 2026, with 350 vials in the City Health Office’s pharmacy and a further 1,179 vials stocked at Rabies Centres across four Denpasar districts. VAR distribution: Denpasar Utara—Puskesmas I 111, Puskesmas II 97, Puskesmas III 135; Denpasar Timur—Puskesmas I 200, Puskesmas II 164; Denpasar Selatan—Puskesmas I 179, Puskesmas II 123, Puskesmas III 56, Puskesmas IV 16; Denpasar Barat—Puskesmas I 27, Puskesmas II 71. Ongoing vaccination campaigns aim to achieve 92.7% coverage of an estimated dog population of 84,369. Continued efforts target reaching unvaccinated dogs to curb rabies transmission in Denpasar City.

article.articleHeadline: Nagan Raya Health Office Team Captures Disease-Carrying Vectors at Several Locations.
article.articleSummary: Two-day vector surveillance by Dinkes Nagan Raya (Aug 21–22, 2026) identified mosquito, fly, and rat vectors in the villages of Lhok Kuala Pesisir, Blang Teungoh, and Ujong Patihah in Kuala District, and Babah Dua in Tadu Raya. Plt Head Hj Syarifah Burhani and disease prevention chief Safrizal supervised the effort to determine vector types, density, and spread to assess transmission risk and guide control measures. Findings indicate vectors capable of transmitting malaria, dengue fever, lymphatic filariasis, chikungunya, diarrhea, and leptospirosis. Breeding sites include waste piles, dense shrubs, and standing water. Community urged to improve environmental cleanliness, proper waste management, and home sanitation. The 24 trained vector surveillance staff, certified by the Ministry of Health, monitor vectors across community health centers within Nagan Raya. No case counts are reported; emphasis remains on prevention and surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Sigi Regency Government forms a task force to tackle tuberculosis cases.
article.articleSummary: TB in Sigi Regency, Central Sulawesi, totals 352 cases as of August 2026. The local government will form a TB Task Force (Satgas TB) to strengthen prevention, case finding, treatment, and contact tracing, aiming for zero TB cases. The plan emphasizes tracing close contacts of each positive case and providing preventive therapy to contacts. The task force will coordinate with Bappeda and be funded by the revised regional budget (APBD Perubahan) while awaiting central support. TB locus tracing integrated with Free Health Check (CKG) operates at 39 sites in Sigi. Nationwide data from Kemendagri show regional disparities: Palu City reports 1,075 TB cases, followed by Parigi Moutong 546 and Banggai 510. These details contextualize local efforts to close gaps in TB detection and management.

article.articleHeadline: Jessica Iskandar and Her Children Briefly Hospitalized Due to Influenza A
article.articleSummary: As of 25 August 2026, Indonesian TV personality Jessica Iskandar and her two children were temporarily hospitalized in Jakarta, Indonesia, after lab-confirmed Influenza A infection was diagnosed in Hagia, followed by Jessica and then son Don. Hagia developed a fever exceeding 41°C with difficulty eating and drinking, prompting hospitalization; Jessica reached about 39.8°C, also requiring care. Don had a fever up to 41°C but remained at home due to good stamina. The family’s illness is suspected to have originated from a nurse, with Hagia first infected, then Jessica, then Don, and subsequently others. Doctors note that Influenza A typically resolves faster than Influenza B. Hagia improved by day four and had no fever for more than 24 hours before discharge, though her mother stayed hospitalized; antiviral treatment continued for five days post-discharge. Don recovered, with only a lingering cough.

article.articleHeadline: Critical Phase of Dengue Fever: Watch Out for Days 3-7 to Prevent Fatalities
article.articleSummary: Critical Phase of Dengue Fever: In Indonesia, the critical phase of dengue begins 3–7 days after fever onset, with the highest risk around days 4–5. Lasting 24–48 hours, this phase involves increased vascular permeability and plasma leakage into body cavities, risking hypovolemic shock. Many families feel relieved when the fever subsides and discharge patients, but the critical phase often starts as the fever wanes. Monitoring is essential per Indonesian guidelines (RI MOH 2024; PAPDI 2023; WHO). Warning signs include severe, persistent abdominal pain; intractable vomiting (especially as fever falls); restlessness or reduced consciousness; sudden bleeding (nosebleeds, gum, hematemesis, melena); cold, clammy extremities with sweating; and signs of shock with a weak, fast pulse. Tests: rising hematocrit (≥20% from baseline) and platelets <100,000/mm³; ultrasound may show free fluid. Treatment: hospital-based IV crystalloids (e.g., Ringer lactate/acetate); possible platelet transfusion for active bleeding. Recovery follows the critical phase.

article.articleHeadline: Alarm over swine fever at the gates of Cerbaie: "Protect pig farms."
article.articleSummary: African swine fever threatens the Cerbaie plateau near Castelfranco, with Altopascio in Lucca province classified as Zone I due to adjacency to affected areas. There are no human cases. Castelfranco’s environment assessor emphasizes coordinating with veterinary authorities and hunters to enforce sanitary rules and protect local pig farms, including small family holdings. The Cerbaie woods span multiple municipalities including Fucecchio, Castelfranco, Santa Croce, Santa Maria a Monte, Calcinaia, Bientina, and Altopascio, and wild boar do not respect borders. Authorities seek to halt transmission along the Arno river and prevent spread to southern communes. The virus originated in Massa-Carrara and has reached Lucca, Pistoia and Prato; the north‑west of Italy is affected, including Piemonte, Valle d'Aosta, Liguria and northwestern Tuscany. If a boar is dead or distressed, do not touch it; note location and call 0573 306655 (daily, 8:00–20:00).

article.articleHeadline: El Niño could lead to an increase in dengue cases and respiratory problems.
article.articleSummary: El Niño, confirmed in June 2026 and likely to persist into early 2027, could raise dengue transmission and respiratory and cardiovascular problems in Brazil. Higher temperatures, drought periods, smoke from fires, and heavier rainfall across regions—more rain in the South, less in the North, Northeast, and Central-West, with above-average temperatures overall—may boost Aedes aegypti proliferation and dehydration risk. In July, Brazil’s Health Ministry warned of potential increases in arboviruses such as dengue and chikungunya; Fiocruz’s InfoDengue projects about 1.7 million dengue cases in 2027, though not a definitive forecast. As of 20 June 2026, dengue had fallen 73% compared with the same period in 2025. Heat exposure can cause dehydration, heat stroke, and cardiac/pulmonary strain, with symptoms like sweating, weakness, dizziness, nausea, headache and cramps; severe signs (confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness) require emergency care. Flooded areas raise risks of leptospirosis, hepatitis A, diarrheal infections, and injuries.

triage.headline_ja: エルニーニョ現象がデング熱および呼吸器系疾患の増加を招く可能性
triage.triage_reason: エルニーニョによる将来的なデング熱等の増加リスクを予測する記事であり、現時点ではデング熱は前年比73%減少している。将来予測に基づく注意喚起であり、緊急のシグナルとは言えないが媒介動物由来感染症の拡大可能性があるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 本記事はエルニーニョ現象による気候変動がデング熱・チクングニア熱・レプトスピラ症・A型肝炎等の増加リスクを予測する将来予測型の記事であり、現状の実発生報告ではない。ブラジル保健省とFiocruzのInfoDengueによる予測に基づく。現時点（2026年6月20日時点）ではデング熱は前年同期比73%減少しているとの記載あり。

article.articleHeadline: Dry Season Raises Alert for Respiratory Infections and Other Diseases in Cuiabá
article.articleSummary: Dry-season conditions in Cuiabá, Mato Grosso—hot, low humidity (humidity index as low as 14–30%, with days under 20% considered critical) and suspended dust—heighten respiratory vulnerability. At Complexo Hospitalar Jardim Cuiabá, respiratory infections are among the top infectious-disease presentations, alongside urinary, gastrointestinal, and skin and soft-tissue infections, with febrile syndromes and hospital-associated infections also monitored. Arboviruses such as dengue and chikungunya continue to circulate, and respiratory viruses including influenza are tracked; tuberculosis remains a key respiratory concern requiring accurate diagnosis. Low humidity can dry mucous membranes and irritate airways, though not all respiratory illness stems from climate. Alarm signs—persistent/high fever, dyspnea, chest pain, hypoxemia, altered consciousness, dehydration, hypotension, reduced urine, bleeding, or rapid deterioration—necessitate urgent care, especially for elderly, pregnant, or immunocompromised individuals. Emphasizes antimicrobial stewardship, and aligns with Anvisa's PNPCIRAS 2026–2030 for prevention, surveillance, and infection-control in healthcare settings.

article.articleHeadline: El Niño triggers an alert for the prevention of vector-borne diseases | Roraima in Focus
article.articleSummary: El Niño-triggered conditions threaten Brazil's vector-borne diseases, with malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and yellow fever under observation. Pan American Health Organization and WHO analyses project that changes in temperature, rainfall, and humidity will reshape mosquito habitats and transmission, varying by region and season. In the Amazon, drought and river recession may expand Anopheles breeding along banks and lagoons during the malaria peak (July–October), while water scarcity increases Aedes aegypti breeding in improvised containers. In Amazonas, 2026 malaria new cases reached 24,437, down 25% from 32,590 in 2025. Dengue shows 425,000 probable cases from Jan 1 to Aug 1, 2026 (week 30), down about 71% year-on-year; El Niño may persist through 2027. Prevention and vaccination remain crucial; vaccines for yellow fever, dengue, and chikungunya are discussed, while malaria and Zika prevention focus on bite avoidance; early diagnosis is essential.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue control campaign finds 98 breeding sites in neighborhoods in the Jardim do Lago region, in Limeira - Portal Veloz
article.articleSummary: Dengue control campaign in Limeira, Brazil, identified 98 dengue breeding sites in Jardim do Lago and neighboring districts during a Saturday operation. The effort involved 93 agents, inspecting 1,583 properties and recording 1,069 as closed, for a total of 2,652 properties assessed across Jardim São João, Jardim Ouro Branco, Jardim Residencial Victório Lucato, Jardim Residencial Roseira, and Jardim do Lago. Among the breeding sites, 34 contained water and 10 harbored larvae, underscoring ongoing Aedes aegypti–related risk. City authorities urged residents to remove water-collecting containers to curb transmission. The initiative aligns with SDG 3—Health and Well-Being, emphasizing prevention, protection of public health, and community participation.

article.articleHeadline: Vaccine startup is the target of the virus investigation at Unicamp.
article.articleSummary: Unicamp in Campinas, São Paulo, is under Federal Police investigation into the disappearance of viral samples linked to AgroTRIX, a vaccine startup founded by Soledad Palameta Miller and Michael Edward Miller. The probe examines whether university resources and academic know-how supported AgroTRIX’s oral vaccines for the agribusiness sector, though there is no proof samples were diverted for private gain. At least 24 viral strains were removed from Unicamp’s Institute of Biology and later located elsewhere on campus, including the Tropical Diseases Laboratory and a -80°C freezer in the Food Engineering faculty. Materials include dengue, Zika, chikungunya, herpes, human coronavirus, and influenza A strains (H1N1, H3N2); a tube labeled “H1N1 - Butantan - PS 23/09/25” was found in a -20°C freezer. Security footage shows Soledad and Michael in restricted areas with PPE lapses. Unicamp has launched a PAD and tightened controls; PF says samples were recovered with no contamination; investigation ongoing.

article.articleHeadline: Ministry of Health reports a rise in Chikungunya with Sidrolândia on alert
article.articleSummary: Sidrolândia, Mato Grosso do Sul, reports 74 probable chikungunya cases between 2 and 15 August 2026, representing 38% of the 194 suspected in the municipality this year. The recent incidence is 157.1 per 100,000, deemed average by SES-MS; the 2026 cumulative rate rises to 411.7 per 100,000, classified as high. Across Mato Grosso do Sul, there are 10,041 probable chikungunya cases, 30 confirmed deaths, and one death under investigation. Dourados accounts for 18 of the deaths, with other cities recording new diagnoses in recent weeks. Chikungunya is transmitted by Aedes aegypti and causes high fever and severe joint pain. Public health guidance urges eliminating standing water, keeping water storage containers closed, and seeking medical care for symptomatic individuals.

article.articleHeadline: Lettuce: What the outbreak with thousands of cases in the United States teaches us about eating greens.
article.articleSummary: An outbreak of cyclosporiasis linked to leafy greens in the United States has surpassed 27,000 confirmed and suspected cases, including 15,716 confirmed and 11,841 under investigation, according to The Independent. The infection is caused by the Cyclospora parasite, with symptoms such as profuse watery diarrhea, cramps, nausea, extreme fatigue, and weight loss. In Brazil, at USP (University of São Paulo), researchers at Esalq/USP and INCT FoRC study factors affecting produce contamination, highlighting how contamination can occur anywhere along the supply chain, often in soil or from inadequately handled organic compost. The current US outbreak is suspected to have originated in vegetable production in Mexico before export to consumers. Emphasis on hygiene: thorough washing of leafy greens at home, leaf-by-leaf; if pre-washed, industry bears responsibility for good practices from field to processing. For at-risk groups, extra caution with raw vegetables, especially outside home.

article.articleHeadline: Understand the brain-eating amoeba that killed an eight-year-old girl.
article.articleSummary: On Aug 22, 2026, an 8-year-old girl in Louisiana died after contracting Naegleria fowleri, the brain-eating amoeba, likely during a swim at Lake Claiborne in Claiborne County. The Louisiana Department of Health confirmed an infection on Aug 19; the family announced the death, noting that brain injuries were too severe for recovery. Naegleria fowleri is a microscopic amoeba found in warm freshwater; infection occurs when water enters the nose, causing primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, a severe inflammation of the brain and meninges. The disease is extremely rare and not contagious person-to-person. CDC data indicate about 180 US infections since 1937. The article also cites a 2024 Brazil case in Ceará (Caucaia), where a 1-year-3-month-old child died from primary amoebic meningoencephalitis acquired from a local reservoir, prompting disinfection. Risk is linked to nasal water entry rather than drinking water; no person-to-person transmission.

article.articleSummary: On August 12, 2026, Cobb-Vantress held the third Pest Control and Biosafety Workshop in Guapiaçu, São Paulo, drawing about 130 professionals from farms, hatcheries, and a feed mill. The event, with internal experts and guests from Elanco and Vetanco, featured a roundtable and a case study to align preventive routines across units and expand biosafety topics beyond 2025. Embrapa guidance was cited, advocating integrated pest management addressing rodents, small pests, flies, and other regional pests, plus humidity reduction and proper composting to curb insect proliferation. The Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock links rodent and insect control to avian influenza prevention, alongside access controls, disinfection, and facility protection. Rafael Bampi, Cobb-Vantress Associate Director of Quality and Sanitation, underscored the need to permanently integrate pest control into all units. The workshop is an annual program.

article.articleHeadline: Child influencer with Down syndrome is hospitalized with a severe infection: 'Emergency'.
article.articleSummary: Eight-year-old influencer Marcello Meninim, who has Down syndrome, was hospitalized in Fortaleza, Ceará, Brazil, after a weekend of vomiting and severe diarrhea. Diagnosed with a severe bacterial infection, he was initially treated for dehydration and later transferred to the ICU for closer monitoring. Initial tests were inconclusive, but repeat analyses confirmed the bacterial infection. As of 25 August 2026, he is recovering, receiving medication, and under observation while awaiting the treatments to take effect. He posted a hospital video to reassure his more than 900,000 followers, thanking supporters and saying he is getting better. His mother, Raquel Cabral, said he remains monitored and medicated; no infection source is disclosed, and no other cases or deaths are reported. The case highlights pediatric infections requiring ICU care.

article.articleHeadline: Meningococcal meningitis: High fatality rate reinforces the urgency of diagnosis and timely vaccination by day 4.
article.articleSummary: Neisseria meningitidis–meningococcal meningitis—poses high fatality risk in Brazil, with 533 meningococcal disease cases and 108 deaths from January to June 2026, per the Ministry of Health. Symptoms include fever, headache, and nausea; neck stiffness may be absent in children under two, while small purplish skin spots and altered mental status can occur. Rapid progression to meningococcemia can happen within 12–24 hours, especially in crowded settings. Diagnosis relies on lumbar puncture with CSF analysis and labs/imaging; early confirmation improves outcomes. Serogroups A, B, C, W, X, and Y exist; vaccines for A, C, W, Y are provided by the National Immunization Program, with meningococcal C vaccine at 3 and 5 months and ACWY boosters at 12 months and for 11–14-year-olds. The private sector offers B vaccines; schedules commonly include 3, 5, 12 months, ACWY boosters at 4–6 years, and two doses of ACWY and B for unvaccinated adolescents.

article.articleHeadline: Regional Electoral Court authorizes institutional campaign to combat dengue during the electoral period
article.articleSummary: Regional Electoral Court of Alagoas authorized an institutional government campaign to prevent and combat dengue, chikungunya, and Zika during the electoral period. The authorization is strictly informative and public-benefit oriented; campaign materials must not display names, symbols, or imagery identifying authorities or public officials, and must omit political promotion. The state remains responsible for ensuring compliance with electoral rules. This decision balances fair electoral competition with the necessity of ongoing public health communication.

article.articleHeadline: Conjunctivitis due to co-infection with adenovirus and influenza
article.articleSummary: In Hanoi, Vietnam, Quang, a one-year-old boy, developed conjunctivitis linked to co-infection with adenovirus and influenza A, alongside bronchitis, rhinitis, and otitis media with inflammation. Bilateral severe conjunctival inflammation featured thick pseudomembranes on the upper and lower eyelids, risking corneal abrasion and impeding drug delivery. The combination of adenovirus and influenza A likely amplified local and systemic inflammation, necessitating up to five membrane removals. Because of the child’s age, membrane peeling required precise, gentle technique to protect the ocular surface; the cornea remained intact and vision preserved. Concurrently, clinicians controlled respiratory symptoms with fever reduction, close breathing monitoring, influenza A antiviral therapy, and antibiotics. After four days, the child improved markedly; within a week, membrane shedding ceased and eyes were clear with no recurrence. Parents should seek prompt ophthalmic evaluation for eye symptoms during viral illnesses, avoid self-administered eye drops (especially corticosteroids), and maintain hand and personal-item hygiene.

The group produced multilingual posters (Korean and English) illustrating Africa’s 54 nations and the domino effect of negative branding. They also opened a global citizen-participation campaign soliciting tips on misused terms via social media with hashtags #Change_ASF and #StopStigma. Collected reports will be forwarded to senior Korean officials (the Blue House, Prime Minister’s Office, and the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs) and media outlets, and VANK will petition WOAH and WHO for formal standardization.

With autumn–winter influenza peaks, vaccination is advised for those six months and older, especially 65+, schoolchildren, people with chronic diseases, frontline workers, and residents of care facilities and schools. Yunnan will offer free or discounted flu vaccines in rural areas; vaccines are available at medical institutions and community centers, with appointments via WeChat channels of Yunnan CDC. Schools and elder-care facilities should enforce screening, ventilation, timely reporting, and vaccination encouragement; seek care for persistent fever or breathing difficulties.

article.articleHeadline: Multi-source agent-based modeling to optimize influenza mitigation strategies in Hong Kong
article.articleSummary: Influenza control in Hong Kong is evaluated via a multi-source, agent-based model across six seasons (2009–2013). The model integrates surveillance, serological, and school absenteeism data to calibrate reported and unreported infections. Compared with baseline strategies, child vaccination targeting under 12 yields the greatest population-level attack-rate reduction, up to 8.5% relative reduction per 100,000 vaccinated. Among non-pharmaceutical interventions, 40% mask coverage lowers attack rates by 18–43%, comparable to 25% of symptomatic individuals staying home. In vaccine-mismatched seasons, combining high-coverage mask use with staying home reduces attack rates by 79–84%. High-coverage school-based vaccination outperforms school closures, reducing student attack rates by up to 85% versus 33% with a 14-day closure. The study provides robust evidence to prioritize child vaccination and strategically combine NPIs to optimize influenza mitigation in Hong Kong.

article.articleHeadline: Incidence and risk factors of Epstein-Barr virus infection and post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder in paediatric haploidentical allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation - Bone Marrow Transplantation
article.articleSummary: From Oct 2022 to Oct 2025 at Peking University People’s Hospital, China, 448 pediatric patients (≤18 years) undergoing ATG-based haploidentical HSCT with letermovir prophylaxis were retrospectively analyzed using 1:3 propensity score matching. EBV viremia occurred in 12.4% and PTLD in 4.9%. Multivariate analysis identified prior CAR-T therapy (HR 2.04; 95% CI 1.061–3.920; p=0.033) and CMV viremia preceding EBV viremia (HR 6.075; 95% CI 3.377–10.928; p<0.001) as risk factors for EBV viremia. PTLD risk was higher with a total body irradiation–based conditioning regimen (HR 1.917; 95% CI 0.980–3.750; p=0.050). Overall survival was similar between EBV+ (92.9%) and EBV− (96.4%; p=0.10), but event-free survival was lower in EBV-infected patients (86.6% vs 94.6%; p=0.004). Chronic GVHD (17.0% vs 6.5%; p<0.001) and transplant-related mortality (7.1% vs 2.1%; p=0.005) were higher in the EBV viremia cohort. Preemptive cytotoxic T lymphocyte therapy may help high-risk individuals.

There is no specific antiviral treatment; management focuses on symptom relief, maintaining fluids, and monitoring for signs of severe disease. Dengue remains common in tropical countries such as the Philippines.

article.articleHeadline: Turning scientific evidence into action for airborne disease control
article.articleSummary: Animation significantly outperformed plain text in motivating preventive health behaviors against airborne infectious diseases. A multi-country study from the Aerosol Science Research Center at National Sun Yat Ysen University (Taiwan), published in Humanities and Social Sciences Communications, involved 3,217 participants across Taiwan, Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines (healthcare professionals, educators, and university students). The researchers compared plain text, explainer comics, and animation using 'The Quest of the Virosols' series and found all formats improved knowledge, but animation produced the strongest behavioral impact, increasing willingness to adopt preventive measures. Animation's advantage stems from emotional engagement through narrative, imagery, and character-driven storytelling, with a notably larger effect among female participants. Implications stress science communication as public health strategy for airborne virus transmission, with resources from the pandemic (COVID-19) now translated into 20 languages to inform global health preparedness.

article.articleHeadline: 386 Die of Dengue as Doctors Warn of Outbreaks, Lack of Vaccine

Cebu City saw 1,228 cases and 10 deaths; Lapu-Lapu had 151 July cases. Zamboanga City declared an August outbreak after 12 deaths from 1,241 cases, with entomological thresholds breached up to 12x. Experts urge vaccination as a supplement to mosquito control, surveillance, and early treatment; reference to second-generation vaccines (TAK-003/Qdenga) being available abroad for consideration in the Philippines.

article.articleHeadline: How dangerous is the Usutu virus?
article.articleSummary: Europe is reporting increasing outbreaks of Usutu virus. Most Usutu infections are asymptomatic, but in some cases, particularly among older adults and immunocompromised individuals, it can cause meningitis, encephalitis, or meningoencephalitis. There have been no Usutu outbreaks in Russia to date, according to MIR24.TV. Separately, Russia has identified an imported case of melioidosis in a woman who returned from Thailand after visiting tours and a farm with elephants; she was hospitalized in serious condition. The article discusses whether melioidosis could trigger an epidemic in Russia, as covered by Vecherny Moskva.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue fever: Can you get sick again after you've had it?
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus with four serotypes (1–4), is described during Thailand’s rainy season, with Aedes mosquitoes as vectors. Infections increasingly involve adolescents and working adults. Classic symptoms include fever (>38°C), severe body aches, nausea/vomiting, loss of appetite, and skin rash with petechiae; some patients have nosebleeds or bleeding gums, and blood may be detected in stool. Laboratory confirmation may reveal low platelets. Dengue typically progresses through three phases: febrile, critical, and recovery; the dangerous phase is the shift from fever to potential shock. Management is supportive: rest, fluids, and acetaminophen; avoid NSAIDs such as ibuprofen and aspirin. If platelets drop after 3–4 days, hospitalization for IV fluids and close monitoring may be needed due to progression to the critical phase. There is no specific antiviral. Vaccines exist but with limited effectiveness; prevention focuses on eliminating mosquito breeding sites, as noted by Ramathibodi Hospital, Mahidol University, Bangkok, Thailand.

article.articleHeadline: Aphthous fever in Lesbos: The sanitary landfill is a public health time bomb again — What the authorities say about the relapse.
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) relapse on Lesbos is linked to improper burial of dead sheep at the island’s landfill (HYTA Lesvou), with insufficient soil cover, lime, and disinfection, raising public-health and environmental concerns. An on-site inspection reported July 24 by the investigative outlet In found major deficiencies: no veterinarian supervising the burial, only two machine operators, no surface disinfection above the pits, minimal lime, and carcasses dumped onto older burial layers with inadequate soil to seal graves. Scavenging crows hover over pits, feeding on exposed carcasses, signaling a potentially dangerous transmission source and possible groundwater contamination. Authorities claimed partial progress from the North Aegean regional governor to supply more soil, but volumes remain insufficient as of August 15, with sheep burials rising again. Lesbos continues reporting cases in Naphi, Pelopi, Agia Paraskevi, Mithymna, Stypsi, and Petra (latest on August 21).

article.articleHeadline: What infections can you contract from tap water in southern countries?
article.articleSummary: Tap water in southern countries poses a major health risk for travelers, with Vietnam, Thailand, and India cited as places where drinking tap water, brushing teeth, and even ice should be avoided. A case report from Krasnoyarsk describes a 23-year-old woman who developed vaginal mucosal inflammation after a trip to Vietnam; local clinicians attributed symptoms to candidiasis but cautioned that water is not a transmission route for sexually transmitted infections, and the medical note cited bacterial vaginosis rather than an STI. Candidiasis can arise from microbiome imbalance, influenced by climate, water, stress, and diet. The article emphasizes that most water‑borne infections are bacterial or parasitic. Enteric bacteria such as E. coli, Salmonella, and Shigella can cause dysentery and traveler's diarrhea; cholera outbreaks occur in India and other Asian countries; Giardia and Cryptosporidium resist chlorination, causing prolonged diarrhea; typhoid fever poses serious risk without prompt treatment.

article.articleHeadline: ‎The Silent Epidemic: How Sexually Transmitted Diseases Are Threatening Ghana's Young Generation ‎
article.articleSummary: Ghana’s STI landscape in 2026 reveals a national prevalence of 7.5%, higher in urban (9.06%) than rural areas (6.67%). Adolescents 15–19 show 7.1% prevalence in males and 12.5% in females. Among 15–24-year-olds, Chlamydia trachomatis dominates at 23.2%, with gonorrhoea 8%, trichomoniasis 7.1%, and Mycoplasma genitalium 1.4%. HIV progress shows a decline from 16,189 new infections in 2024 to 13,951 in 2025, but 38–42 daily infections and more than 107,000 people living with HIV remain unaware. Youth aged 15–24 account for 27.5% of new HIV infections, while 2022 DHS indicates low condom use and a gap between knowledge and practice. Northern regions face cultural barriers; Oxfam Ghana’s Power to Choose targets 10–24-year-olds across several regions, though progress toward Agenda 2030 remains incomplete.

article.articleHeadline: The dangers of keeping exotic pets, according to a biologist: "The risk of zoonosis is very high."
article.articleSummary: Exotic pets are increasingly common in Europe, especially Spain, including iguanas, snakes, bearded dragons, Florida turtles, Gambian giant rats, African hedgehogs, raccoons, and some primates. A Savanta ComRes survey for Eurogroup for Animals shows 87% of Europeans oppose keeping exotic species as pets. The trade, legal and illegal, threatens biodiversity and animal welfare, with high mortality during transport. Zoonoses pose the greatest risk among reptiles and amphibians, exotic rodents, and primates. In the United States, a 2022 CDC report links outbreaks to non-traditional pets with diseases such as salmonellosis, rat-bite fever, lymphocytic choriomeningitis, Seoul virus, and mpox in primates. Reptiles in captivity nearly universally carry Salmonella; Ontario studies tie rising human salmonellosis to reptiles. The Gambian giant rat is linked to mpox outbreaks; in 2003, 71 people were infected via Ghana-imported rats. Spain’s 2022 mpox outbreak affected thousands, with some fatalities. Recommendation: avoid purchasing exotic animals to reduce zoonosis risk and protect biodiversity.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, the WHO confirms the international emergency: "Low risk for third countries, no to border closures"
article.articleSummary: Outbreak: Ebola virus Bundibugyo in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). After the WH0 Emergency Committee’s second meeting (18 Aug), temporary recommendations published 24 Aug keep third-country risk as 'low' with no border closures or flight suspensions. The event is confirmed as a PHEIC but not a pandemic. In the DRC, risk is 'very high'; neighboring countries (Angola, Burundi, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia) face 'high' regional risk. By 16 Aug MSF reports >5,000 cases and >2,400 deaths; WHO notes nearly 5,000 cases and >2,300 deaths in total, with deaths in the past week ≈ one every 30 minutes. The outbreak is the largest, fastest Ebola epidemic in DRC history, with many deaths at home. WHO urges strengthened case finding, rapid alert investigation, expanded diagnostics, 21‑day contact follow‑up, rapid isolation, nearby treatment centers, trained staff, and safe burials; Uganda's response is highlighted, and a July imported French case is noted, underscoring vigilance at entry points.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、WHOが国際的緊急事態を確認：「第三国へのリスクは低い、国境封鎖は行わない」
triage.triage_reason: WHOがコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクをPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）として再確認し、史上最大・最速のエボラ流行かつ多数の死亡例が報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため、フルリスク評価に進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラ流行がPHEICとして確認された状況を報じている。近隣国（アンゴラ、ブルンジ、中央アフリカ、コンゴ共和国、ルワンダ、南スーダン、タンザニア、ウガンダ、ザンビア）は『地域リスク高』とされているが、実際の症例発生国としてはDRCのみが記事内で明示されている。ザンビアは対象国リストに含まれるが、感染発生ではなく地域リスクとしての言及のみのため、verified_locationsには含めなかった。フランスでの輸入例（7月）も言及されているが対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: Central Africa intensifies controls in response to a new hemorrhagic fever emergency - HSB News
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by Bundibugyo virus, has expanded to six provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Upper Uele, Tshopo, and Bas-Uele. As of August 14, 2026, the outbreak reports 4,665 laboratory-confirmed cases and 2,184 deaths; by August 24, reports exceed 5,500 cases and over 2,600 deaths. The WHO notes this is the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and warns transmission is spreading geographically. Regional cross-border coordination is urged; at-risk neighbors include the Central African Republic, Republic of Congo, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, Tanzania, Zambia, and Angola, with enhanced surveillance, border and community monitoring, investigation of unexplained deaths, and rapid notification. Early symptoms can mimic other diseases; two-thirds of deaths occurred in communities rather than treatment centers, underscoring access and security barriers.

triage.headline_ja: 中央アフリカ、新たな出血熱の緊急事態に対応し警戒を強化
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で発生したエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）がDRC史上最大規模の流行となり、6州に拡大、5,500例以上・死亡2,600例以上を記録。国境を越えた拡大リスクが高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: 記事中の周辺国（ザンビア、ウガンダ、ルワンダ等）は『リスクにさらされている隣国』として言及されているのみで、実際の感染確認地域ではないため verified_locations には含めていない。DRC国内の大規模かつ史上最大のエボラ流行であり、越境拡大の懸念が高い重大シグナル。
